subject: Adding a custom legend in ggplot

messages.author: 4f95944ce785e8db
messages.subject: Adding a custom legend in ggplot
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to add a legend without using any of the variable from the dataset. I have searched on different forums but I couldn't find anywhere on adding a custom legend. I am attaching an example code below. It'd be great if someone can help me add a legend to the graph below such that I can say symbols are "X" and the line is "Y". 

Thanks a bunch for your help,
Vaishali 

library(ggplot2)
x <- sample(1:100, 25)
y <- sample(1:100, 25)

data <- data.frame(x=x, y=y)
trial <- ggplot() +  
  geom_point(data=data, aes(x=x, y=y), shape=1, color="red") +
  geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1, size=0.7)

messages.author: f20966e9bc9cf5c7
messages.subject: Re: Adding a custom legend in ggplot
parts:
Hello Vaishali,

you must have data with a variable that has more than one category,
which are then mapped to a different color, linetype, or the like. Once
your data visualization has this property, a legend will be drawn
automatically, which you can then modify, according to the aesthetic to
which you've mapped. (I guess i screwed up the terminology.)

There are many introductions in the internet. You have to get away from
the thinking of how to plot in base R.

Please start here (I like this one):
http://www.noamross.net/blog/2012/10/5/ggplot-introduction.html

Cheers,
Brian
